items.abstract: <jats:p>Audio-language models (LALMs) condition generation on acoustic evidence that transcripts do not encode, including source characteristics, speaker overlap, replay, masking, and room acoustics. These cues can determine whether an instruction should be followed, refused, or clarified. Transcription-first defenses discard such evidence, whereas model-wide refusal steering can degrade benign listening. We introduce Cross-Modal Safety-Component Steering, a white-box inference-time defense that estimates component-specific safety directions from matched probes, ranks candidates by intervention evidence and benign sensitivity, and applies calibrated updates only at selected audio-conditioned states during early generation. We evaluate Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct and MOSS-Audio-8B-Instruct on six non-adaptive attack families and three benign listening tasks. We additionally evaluate Qwen2-Audio under held-out acoustic shifts and a white-box adaptive attack. Local steering lowers attack success rate (ASR) from 25.4% to 10.4% on Qwen2-Audio and from 23.8% to 12.1% on MOSS-Audio, while achieving 96.1% and 95.3% benign utility preservation (BUP), respectively. On Qwen2-Audio, the local-steering wrapper adds 1.6 ms median overhead, and conditional gating raises BUP to 97.5%. Under defense-specific adaptive optimization, routed steering lowers ASR from 38.8% to 23.8%. These results demonstrate that sparse, architecture-aware intervention materially strengthens LALM jailbreak resistance while preserving general audio capabilities.</jats:p>
title: Cross-Modal Safety-Component Steering for Audio-Language Model Jailbreak Defense

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Cross-domain recommendation offers a potential avenue for alleviating data sparsity and cold-start problems. Embedding and mapping, as a classic cross-domain research genre, aims to identify a common mapping function to perform representation transformation between two domains via exploiting the supervision signals of overlapping users. Nevertheless, coarse-grained preference representations, non-personalized mapping functions, and excessive reliance on overlapping users limit their performance, especially in scenarios where overlapping users are sparse. To address the aforementioned challenges, we propose a novel
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">
                      <jats:bold>C</jats:bold>
                    </jats:italic>
                    ross-domain transfer of
                    <jats:bold>V</jats:bold>
                    alence
                    <jats:bold>P</jats:bold>
                    references via a
                    <jats:bold>M</jats:bold>
                    eta-optimization approach, namely
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">
                      <jats:bold>CVPM</jats:bold>
                    </jats:italic>
                    .
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">CVPM</jats:italic>
                    formalizes cross-domain interest transfer as a hybrid architecture of parametric meta-learning and self-supervised learning, which not only enables a more nuanced transfer of user preferences but also enhances signal quality by incorporating insights from non-overlapping users. Specifically, drawing on in-depth knowledge into user preferences and valence preference theory, we believe that there exists a significant difference between users’ positive preferences and negative behaviors, and thus employ differentiated encoders to learn their distributions. In particular, we further utilize the pre-trained model and item popularity to sample pseudo-interaction items to ensure the integrity of both distributions. To guarantee the personalized preference transfer, we treat each user’s mapping as two parts, the common transformation and the personalized bias, where the network generating the personalized bias is produced by a meta-learner. Furthermore, beyond the supervised loss for overlapping users, we design contrastive tasks for non-overlapping users from both group and individual levels to avoid model skew and enhance the semantic richness of representations. We construct six cross-domain tasks and one cross-system task from 10 data sets assessing model performance under both cold-start and warm-start scenarios. Exhaustive data analysis and extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and advancement of our proposed framework.
                  </jats:p>
title: Cross-domain Transfer of Valence Preferences via a Meta-optimization Approach
